points.t: A **firm, slowly enlarging plaque** on the trunk or shoulder that later becomes **lumpy (protuberant)**.
Low-grade fibroblastic sarcoma driven by a **COL1A1–PDGFB** fusion.
Refer on a **suspected sarcoma / skin-cancer pathway**; deep biopsy; Mohs or wide excision; **imatinib** for inoperable disease.
**Delayed diagnosis** because it is called a scar, keloid or dermatofibroma for years.

cause.lead: A fusion gene that drives PDGF signalling.
points: > 90%: **t(17;22)** (often ring chromosome) → **COL1A1–PDGFB** → autocrine PDGF receptor stimulation (imatinib rationale).
Histology: storiform spindle cells infiltrating fat (‘honeycomb’); **CD34 +, Factor XIIIa −**.

visuals.caption: DFSP over years: a firm scar-like plaque enlarges and later becomes protuberant and multinodular.
visuals.alt: Three shoulders showing a plaque growing into a nodular mass

points: Adults 20–50; **trunk (chest, shoulder)**, proximal limbs, head and neck.
Starts as a firm skin-coloured, pink-violet or brown **indurated plaque** (‘scar’, ‘keloid’, ‘morphoea’, ‘DF’).
Variants: pigmented (Bednar), atrophic (morphoea-like), childhood; can mimic keloidal BCC.
MRI for large / recurrent tumours; chest imaging only if fibrosarcomatous / metastatic.

cards.name: Keloid / hypertrophic scar
cards.clue: Injury history: beware a ‘keloid’ without one.

manage.lead: IP role: suspicion and referral only.

points: Enlarging ‘scar’, ‘keloid’ or ‘DF’, > 2–3 cm, or nodular on the trunk → **urgent** dermatology (skin cancer or sarcoma pathway; NG12 sarcoma route if access is slow).
**Margin-controlled surgery** (Mohs / slow Mohs) preferred (EORTC / EADO) over WLE with 2–3 cm margins.
Radiotherapy for positive margins that can’t be re-excised.
CYP3A4 interactions; warfarin; caution with high-dose paracetamol.

items.t: A ‘dermatofibroma’ or ‘keloid’ that keeps growing, is > ~3 cm or becomes nodular: exclude **DFSP**.

pearls.t: “A keloid **without an injury** is not a keloid until proved otherwise.”
DFSP: CD34 +, Factor XIIIa − (DF the reverse).
Shave biopsy misses it: biopsy deep.
